explanation: The illustration and headline-writing steps were appropriate, and text-overlay was suitable for this simple social headline. The final step supplied a rendering instruction instead of binding the actual headline as its text, so the tool printed the instruction and its oversized panel obscured the scene. The catalogue’s warning about image-model lettering did not cause this failure; correctly parameterized text-overlay would have worked.
better_chain: image (square beach-cleanup illustration with clear headline space) → write (short English headline) → text-overlay (set text explicitly to “Love Your Beach? Lend a Hand!” in a compact, high-contrast top band) → check (confirm headline, square format, visible cleanup activity, and no dates or signup details)

steps.issue: The text parameter needed the literal headline, not an instruction referring to headline.txt. Passing the file alongside the image did not populate that parameter; the instruction itself was rendered, creating an oversized panel.
